content.Table_Title: Pharmacological Characteristics of Available Antiarrhythmic Medications for Treating VA

Medications.Dose: PO 200-1200 mg daily or up to 600 mg bid
Medications.Electrophysiological Effects: Sinus rate slowed, AV nodal refractoriness increased
Medications.Pharmacological Characteristics: Active metabolite t1/2: 8–13 h, Prolonged with renal impairment, Metab H: H, Excr: F 60%, U 40%
Medications.Common Adverse Effects: Cardiac: Bradycardia, hypotension, HF, AVB; Other: Dizziness, fatigue, anxiety, impotence, hyper/ hypothesisa

Medications.Dose: IV: 300 mg bolus for VF/pulseless VT arrest; 150 mg bolus for stable VT; 1 mg/min x 6 h, then 0.5 mg/min x 18 h. PO: 400 mg 2 to 3 times daily for 1–2 wk, then 300–400 mg daily; reduce dose to 200 mg daily if possible
Medications.Target: I_b, I_to, I_Kr, I_Ks, I_K1, Beta receptor, Alpha receptor nuclear T3 receptor
Medications.Electrophysiological Effects: Sinus rate slowed, QRS prolonged, QTc prolonged, AV nodal refractoriness increased; increased DFT
Medications.Pharmacological Characteristics: t1/2: 26–107 d, Metab H: H, Excr: F
Medications.Common Adverse Effects: Cardiac: Hypotension, bradycardia, AVB, TdP, slows VF below programmed ICD detection rate, increases defibrillation threshold; Other: Corneal microdeposits, thyroid abnormalities, ataxia, nausea, emesis, constipation, photosensitivity, skin discoloration, ataxia, dizziness, peripheral neuropathy, tremor, hepatitis, cirrhosis, pulmonary fibrosis or pneumonitis
